title: Vectors, Matrices & Operations
motto: Every neural network is just matrix multiplication with extra steps.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: Every neural network is just matrix multiplication with extra steps.

steps.title: Why shapes matter
cards: In PyTorch you see output = weights @ input + bias. That @ is matrix multiplication — the entire forward pass of a layer in three operations.
If inner dimensions do not match, you get a shape error. (128×784) @ (784×1) = (128×1) is valid because 784 = 784.

steps.title: Matrix multiply transforms space
steps.body: Matrix multiplication combines rows of A with columns of B via dot products. Element-wise multiply is different — same shape, multiply matching positions. Neural networks use @, not *.

steps.title: Implement matrix_multiply
steps.body: Write matrix_multiply(A, B) for matrices represented as lists of lists. No numpy. Inner dimensions must match or raise ValueError.

code.starter:
def matrix_multiply(A, B):
    """Return A @ B for matrices as list-of-lists."""
    rows_a = len(A)
    cols_a = len(A[0]) if rows_a else 0
    rows_b = len(B)
    cols_b = len(B[0]) if rows_b else 0
    if cols_a != rows_b:
        raise ValueError("inner dimensions must match")
    # TODO: compute each output[i][j] as dot(row i of A, col j of B)
    return [[0 for _ in range(cols_b)] for _ in range(rows_a)]
